title: When to go to Nepal: seasons, monsoon and altitude
meta_description: Best time to visit Nepal: month-by-month seasons for Kathmandu, Pokhara and treks, monsoon rain-shadow options, and how to handle altitude above 3,000 m.
summary: October and November are Nepal's best months, with clear skies over every trail. March and April are the second peak, with rhododendrons and warmer days. December to February suits the valley and low treks. The monsoon, June to August, is for the rain-shadow north around Marpha and Lo Manthang, and for city festivals.

sections.heading: Nepal's four seasons in one paragraph each
paras: Autumn, from late September to November, is the classic season. The monsoon has washed the air clean, the big peaks are visible from dawn into the afternoon, and the rice terraces turn gold. It is also when Nepal's two biggest festivals, Dashain and Tihar, fall. Everything is busy: Lukla flights, teahouses on the Everest and Annapurna trails and lakeside hotels in Pokhara.

Winter, from December to February, is cold and very clear in the hills. Kathmandu drops to around 2 °C at night but warms to the high teens by day, and Pokhara stays mild. Low treks such as Poon Hill are excellent, if cold at Ghorepani. Above about 4,000 m, nights fall well below freezing and some lodges close.

Spring, from March to May, warms quickly. Rhododendron forests flower on the Annapurna foothills in March and April, and the Everest climbing season builds through April and May. Afternoon haze and cloud grow week by week, so mountain views are best early. Valley cities get hot by late May.

Summer, June to August, is the monsoon. Rain falls most afternoons and nights, leeches appear on mid-altitude trails, landslides close roads, and Lukla flights are often cancelled. But the north side of the Himalaya, in Upper Mustang and the upper Kali Gandaki, lies in a rain shadow and stays mostly dry.

sections.heading: Month by month at a glance
paras: This table rates each month for the three kinds of trip most people plan. Ratings are for a typical year; the monsoon can arrive or leave a couple of weeks early or late.

sections.heading: The monsoon and the rain shadow
paras: The monsoon usually reaches eastern Nepal in early June and the whole country by mid-June, withdrawing in the second half of September. Pokhara, sitting right under the Annapurna range, receives some of the heaviest rainfall in Nepal. On the Prithvi Highway between Kathmandu and Pokhara and on the road up the Kali Gandaki to Jomsom, landslides can close traffic for hours or days.

Travel north of the main range and the picture changes. The Annapurna and Dhaulagiri massifs block most of the monsoon cloud, so Marpha, Jomsom and Upper Mustang get little rain. Marpha's apple orchards ripen from August, and Upper Mustang is green at the edges of its barley fields. Getting there is the problem: the Jomsom flight is often cancelled in monsoon cloud, and the road from Beni can be blocked. Build in spare days.

The monsoon is also festival season in the Kathmandu valley. Gai Jatra in August and Indra Jatra in September fill the Durbar Squares, and the temples are quiet between them. If your dates are fixed in summer, a valley culture trip or an Upper Mustang trek is the honest recommendation.
list: Carry a rain cover for your pack and a dry bag for documents and electronics.
Keep one spare day in every monsoon itinerary for road or flight delays.
Check road and flight status each morning; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Altitude: how high you will sleep
paras: Most of Nepal's popular places are low. Kathmandu is at 1,400 m, Pokhara at about 820 m, Bandipur at about 1,030 m and Nagarkot at about 2,175 m. Ghandruk is at about 2,000 m and Ghorepani at 2,860 m. Altitude is not usually a problem at these heights, though some people notice a mild headache or poorer sleep around 2,800 m.

It becomes real at Namche Bazaar, 3,440 m, and Lo Manthang, about 3,840 m. Above about 2,500 m, the body needs time to adapt to lower oxygen, and the usual rule is to raise your sleeping altitude by no more than 300–500 m a day once above 3,000 m, with a rest day every two or three days. On the Everest trail, that is why trekkers spend two nights at Namche before going higher.

Acute mountain sickness feels like a hangover: headache, nausea, loss of appetite, dizziness and poor sleep. If it gets worse rather than better, the answer is to stop climbing and, if needed, go down. Breathlessness at rest, confusion or loss of balance are danger signs that need immediate descent. Talk to your doctor before the trip about your health and whether medication such as acetazolamide is right for you.
list: Walk slowly, especially on the first climbing days.
Drink enough water and avoid alcohol for the first nights above 3,000 m.
Climb high and sleep low: day walks above your lodge help you adjust.
Tell your guide early about any symptom; guides are trained to watch for them.
Carry travel insurance that covers trekking altitude and helicopter evacuation.

sections.heading: Festivals worth timing a trip around
paras: Nepal's festival calendar is a good reason to pick a month. Bisket Jatra in Bhaktapur marks Nepali New Year in mid-April with chariot pulling between the upper and lower halves of the town. Tiji brings three days of masked dances to Lo Manthang, usually in May. Indra Jatra in Kathmandu, usually in September, takes the living goddess Kumari through the old city in her chariot.

Dashain, usually in late September or October, is Nepal's biggest festival, with families gathering for tika and blessings over about fifteen days. Tihar, the festival of lights, follows a few weeks later. Both are wonderful to see, but buses and flights fill, some shops and offices close, and prices rise. Book transport well ahead and expect a slower pace for a few days. Festival dates follow lunar calendars, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Crowds, prices and booking ahead
paras: Season shapes price as much as weather. In October, April and the Christmas–New Year week, Pokhara's lakeside rooms, Kathmandu's better hotels and the teahouses at Ghorepani and Namche fill early, and rates rise by a third or more. Lukla flights for late October are often sold weeks ahead, and in peak months many of them leave from Ramechhap (Manthali), about four hours' drive from Kathmandu, which adds a very early start.

In December, January and February, and again in late May and September, you can usually find rooms on arrival, guides have more choice of dates and lodges are quieter. For Indian travellers, Diwali and school holidays bring families to Pokhara and Nagarkot, so those weeks book up even when foreign arrivals are low. Dashain and Tihar also fill buses heading out of Kathmandu for several days.

sections.heading: Our pick by type of traveller
paras: If you have a choice of dates, these are the months we suggest.
list: First trip, cities and Pokhara: October, November, February or March.
Poon Hill and Ghandruk: late March to mid-April for flowers, October to November for clear views.
Namche and the Everest region: October to November, or April to May.
Upper Mustang and Marpha: April to October, including the monsoon.
Families with children: October to December, or the February school break.
Lowest prices with decent weather: late November, December, January and February.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Nepal?
faqs.a: October is the best single month, with clear skies after the monsoon, comfortable temperatures and every trail open. November is almost as good and less crowded by the end. March and April are the next best, with rhododendrons on the trails. Book flights and rooms early for all four months.

faqs.q: Is it worth visiting Nepal in the monsoon?
faqs.a: For the Kathmandu valley's festivals and temples, or for treks in the rain-shadow north such as Upper Mustang and the upper Kali Gandaki around Marpha, yes. For views and treks south of the main range, no: cloud, rain, leeches and landslides make June to August a poor time. Keep spare days for delays.

faqs.q: How cold is Nepal in December and January?
faqs.a: Kathmandu falls to around 2–4 °C at night and reaches 18–20 °C on sunny afternoons. Pokhara is milder. Ghorepani on the Poon Hill trail drops below freezing at night, and Namche Bazaar falls to about −8 to −10 °C. Many guesthouses have no central heating, so pack warm layers.

faqs.q: When is the best time to trek to Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a: October and November are the most reliable, with clear skies and stable weather. April and May are also good, with warmer days and the climbing season under way, though afternoon cloud is more common. December to February is possible for well-equipped trekkers but very cold, and some lodges close.

faqs.q: Will I get altitude sickness in Kathmandu or Pokhara?
faqs.a: Very unlikely. Kathmandu is at 1,400 m and Pokhara at about 820 m, well below the height where altitude sickness usually starts. It becomes a real risk on treks that sleep above about 3,000 m, such as Namche Bazaar or Lo Manthang. Talk to your doctor before any high trek.

faqs.q: When does the monsoon start and end in Nepal?
faqs.a: It usually arrives in mid-June and withdraws in the second half of September, with July and August the wettest months. Timing varies by a week or two each year. By early October, trails have usually dried out and the skies are clear.

faqs.q: When can I see rhododendrons in Nepal?
faqs.a: On the Poon Hill and Ghandruk trails, the forests between about 2,500 m and 3,200 m flower from March to mid-April, with red, pink and white blooms. Lower down they start earlier, and higher up a little later. Laligurans, the red rhododendron, is Nepal's national flower.

faqs.q: Is it good to visit Nepal during Dashain?
faqs.a: It is a good time to see family life and festival markets, and the weather is usually excellent. But buses fill, fares rise, some offices and shops close for days, and many Nepalis travel home. Book transport early and plan a relaxed itinerary around the main days. Check current status of dates before you travel.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Nepal in October?
faqs.a: Light layers for sunny days in Kathmandu and Pokhara, a fleece and a warm jacket for mornings, a down jacket if trekking above 3,000 m, a rain shell, sunscreen and sunglasses. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for the Durbar Squares' old paving and for trails.
